subject: Plan architecture: seat vs throughput — downgrade & bundling options
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pulsartech.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Plan architecture: seat vs throughput — initial ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the time last week. We're trying to map out a practical packaging approach for PulsarTech's AI assistant use case and want to understand Redwood's downgrade/upgrade behavior and feature bundling tradeoffs before the procurement review. A few things we need clarified:

- Our traffic profile: spiky inference (50k tokens/day baseline, spikes to 1.2M tokens on product launches).
- Main blockers: predictable spend during spikes, keeping latency under 300ms P95 for user-facing flows, and retaining access to embeddings for search.

Specific questions:
1) If we choose a seat-based plan with burst credits, how does proration work if we step down mid-quarter?
2) Are quantization recommendations (low-precision variants) considered an add-on or included when we move to a higher tier?
3) Can we bundle embeddings as a capped add-on to avoid surprise overages?

I've attached a draft SOW and a small usage sample for context. Can we do a 30-minute call to go over a recommendation matrix and a conservative cost estimate?

Appreciate it —
Sanjay Rao
Director of Data Products
PulsarTech
Attachment: Pulsar_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pulsartech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Plan architecture: seat vs throughput — initial ask

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear summary and the SOW — that's helpful. Quick answers first, then propose next steps: 

1) Proration and step-downs: we offer a monthly proration model for seat reductions. If you step down mid-billing period we credit the unused commitment pro rata toward the next invoice. For reserved capacity (Dedicated) we require a 30-day notice and typically negotiate a runway for committed GPU pools.

2) Quantization: recommendations themselves are advisory and included in Redwood Optimize, but applying a quantized model variant to live traffic is effectively a model variant change. Higher tiers include a set of supported quantized variants; for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can include an agreed quantization profile as part of the commit.

3) Embeddings bundling: yes — we can set a capped embeddings add-on. We typically structure it as a token-cap with an overage rate (or a fixed monthly bucket).

Recommended next steps:
- Short call to align on cost bounds and risk profile (30 min).
- I'll prepare two scenarios: (A) Seat-first with burst credits + capped embeddings, (B) Throughput-first (predictable reserved capacity) with model-variant fallbacks.
- Early recommendation: for your spiky pattern, Seat-first + burst credits is lower upfront and easier to trial; Dedicated is better if you want strict P95 guarantees and data isolation.

Available slots tomorrow 10–12 PT or Friday 9–11 PT — which works?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Plan architecture: seat vs throughput — downgrade & bundling options

Kim / Lauren —

Looping in our recommended commercial structure based on Pulsar's usage sample and the ask in Alyssa's note. This is an internal note (don't forward externally until we align):

Recommendation summary:
- Option A (Seat-first, conservative): Seat-Plus (baseline 10 seats) + monthly 200k token burst bucket + capped embeddings add-on (500k tokens). Suggested discount: 10% on list for a 6-month commit. 6-month ARR-equivalent locked, proration for seat reductions (standard).
- Option B (Throughput-first): Dedicated reserved pool sized for 1.0M tokens/day peak with automatic fallback to Seat-Plus for overflow. Suggested discount: 18% on list for a 12-month committed cadence, with SLA credits tied to observed latency.

Commercial notes:
- If procurement needs a firm downgrade runway, we can add a 60-day soft-commit clause (reductions permitted with a 60-day notice and adjusted crediting schedule) — this preserves capacity planning.
- Quantization tagging: recommend including a "quantization validation" milestone in the SOW (we own the rollout assistance; Pulsar signs off on rollback criteria).
- Embeddings: cap as an add-on with a fixed monthly bucket; any overage billed at a pre-agreed rate (list * 0.015).

Next steps suggested for the call:
1) Kimberly: present Option A & B slide with 6-month P&Ls and the step-down runway language.
2) Lauren: prepare a draft term amendment for the 60-day soft-commit clause.
3) I will propose the discount bands above and prepare a short negotiation playbook (what concessions to trade for longer commit).

HubSpot deal: HSP-98372 (assign owner after call).

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
